answer.rationale: The incumbent has refused to reopen price this cycle, so renewing or negotiating won't meet the 18% mandate, and the contract's imminent expiration (14 days, no auto-renew) forces a decision now rather than deferring. The low-cost vendor's quote meets the cost mandate outright, and memory_c2 indicates a prior switch to this type of vendor was smooth (quick onboarding, accurate invoicing), which supports feasibility. However, running at 94% of committed volume with zero buffer means any onboarding friction or early supply hiccup with a new primary vendor could breach delivery commitments, so I want to verify the original c2 record for onboarding timeline specifics and cross-check c1 (incumbent renewal stability) before fully committing at broad scale. I'm treating this as a standard, closely monitored transition rather than an unguarded full rollout, and explicitly flagging the delivery-risk tradeoff rather than assuming last cycle's smooth onboarding will repeat under tighter capacity conditions.
